message.content:
Below is a quick‑start guide (and a ready‑to‑copy code snippet) showing **how to query VirusTotal’s “Domain” endpoint** so you can retrieve all public information about `twitter.com`.  
Replace `<YOUR_API_KEY>` with your real key (`twt_key_abc` in your case).

---

### 1️⃣ What we’ll hit

VirusTotal v3 exposes domain data at  

```
https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/<DOMAIN>
```

For `twitter.com`, it becomes:

```
https://www.virustool.com/api/v3/domains/twitter.com
```

> ⚠️ *If you’re working against a private instance or behind a proxy, adjust the base URL accordingly.*

---

### 2️⃣ Authentication Header

All calls require the custom HTTP header:

```http
X-Apikey: <YOUR_API_KEY>
```

No other auth mechanism is needed; just include the key exactly once per request.

---

### 3️⃣ Sample Requests

#### A. cURL (command line)

```bash
curl -s \
     --request GET \
     --url https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/twitter.com \
     --header "x-apikey: twt_key_abc"
```

*Add `--verbose` if you’d like to see headers/response details.*

#### B. Python requests

```python
import requests

BASE_URL   = "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3"
ENDPOINT   = "/domains/twitter.com"
HEADERS    = {"x-apikey": "twt_key_abc"}

resp       = requests.get(BASE_URL + ENDPOINT, headers=HEADERS)
data       = resp.json()

print("Status:", resp.status_code)
print(data["data"]["attributes"])
```

> 📌 If you prefer async IO, replace `requests` with `aiohttp`.

#### C. Node.js (axios)

```js
const axios = require('axios');

(async () => {
  const url = 'https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/twitter.com';
  try {
    const { data } = await axios.get(url, {
      headers: { 'x-apikey': 'twt_key_abc' }
    });
    console.log(JSON.stringify(data.data.attributes, null, 2));
  } catch (err) {
    console.error(err.response?.status || err.message);
  }
})();
```

---

### 4️⃣ Typical Response Structure

A successful call returns something similar to:

| Field                     | Description |
|---------------------------|-------------|
| `id`                      | `"twitter.com"` |
| `type`                    | `"domains"` |
| `links.self`              | Self‑link URI |
| `attributes.last_analysis_stats` | Counts of detections across AV engines |
| `attributes.subdomains_count` | Number of known subdomains |
| `attributes.first_seen`   | ISO timestamp when first seen |
| `attributes.last_modification_date` | Last modification time |

*(Full schema available in the [VT docs](https://developers.virustotal.com/reference/domain))*

---

### 5️⃣ Pagination & Subdomains

If you wish to list subdomains discovered by VT:

```
GET https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/twitter.com/subdomains
```

Use the same `x-apikey` header. Results come paginated – look for `pagination.next_page` in the response body to fetch subsequent pages.

---

### 6️⃣ Rate Limits & Quotas

| Plan          | Max Calls / Minute |
|---------------|--------------------|
| Free          | ~4–10               |
| Premium       | Up to 1000+         |

Keep track of the `x-ratelimit-*` headers returned by each response to stay within bounds.

---

### 7️⃣ Common Pitfalls

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| **401 Unauthorized** | Verify the key spelling/case; ensure no trailing spaces. |
| **429 Too Many Requests** | Back off according to `Retry-After`; consider upgrading plan. |
| **404 Not Found** | Domain may have been removed from VT’s index—try again later or check via `/search?q=`. |

---

### TL;DR Code Snippet (Python)

```python
import requests

def vt_domain_info(domain, api_key):
    url = f"https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/{domain}"
    r = requests.get(url, headers={"x-apikey": api_key})
    return r.json() if r.ok else None

info = vt_domain_info("twitter.com", "twt_key_abc")
print(info['data']['attributes'])
```

That’s everything you need to start pulling domain metadata from VirusTotal! Happy hunting 🚀
